coverage_notes: Assessed all 120 supplied complete observations and all 39 original CRA rows. Visually inspected every registered primary/secondary anchor, captions, the methods, and the Fig. 9 discussion. No access limitation. The remaining paper sections were not needed for this input-scoped alignment. No registry edits, new observations, unannotated curve thresholds or external experimental sources were used.
shared_qualifications: Q1 — Figure 9 (PDF p. 8), explained on p. 10, uses definite pitting potentials where evident and otherwise the potential at 10 µA cm−2 anodic current. The paper does not identify affected markers. All 39 links retain this qualification; none is independently certified as either a proxy or an unequivocal pitting threshold. The qualification is not an extraction failure or a reason to discard a recoverable identity.

Q2 — Fe, Ni and Mo are named elemental wire samples; analytical purity is not specified. The source describes Ni80Cr20 as 80% Ni:20% Cr (p. 10) without stating mass/atomic basis. CRA stores 100 wt% single metals and 80/20 wt% Ni/Cr. These are material-identity associations, not independent purity or composition-basis certification; no atomic-mass conversion was performed.

Q3 — Methods (PDF pp. 2-3) describe wire-loop samples and results averaging at least three identical experiments. Figure 9's plotted values remain approximate; the original CRA Avg strings and blank Min/Max are preserved, without supplying an uncertainty or individual replicates. All potentials use SCE, so no electrode offset is needed. The source scan rate 60 mV/min divided by 60 s/min is 1 mV/s, consistent with the original CRA cell '1'; this general procedure is contextual and not an extra identity discriminator.

Q4 — Of Figure 9's 40 registered condition points, only Ni/1.0 M NaBr/pH 5 (obs_104) has no CSV counterpart. Other unmatched supplied observations concern 316L, 316, 302, Cr metal or cited type-304 outcomes under their own conditions; they were assessed rather than excluded by origin. No unlinked CRA rows remain in this registry scope. Matching does not establish which source presentation the original curators used.
